brief: France's widening OAT/Bund spread is pressuring the SX5E toward its 6200 make-or-break level, which is also breaking its 100-day moving average and testing its long-term trendline. European equity vol (V2X) is spiking but still lags the bigger move in credit stress (iTraxx Main). The euro is at its most oversold since 2015, and French rate stress has spread into Italian yields. TS Lombard argues Europe, especially France (Japan's largest individual European sovereign holding after USTs), may be more exposed than the US at the margin to Japanese capital pulling back, since JGB yields now exceed hedged DM bond yields; Lombard expects a more active BoJ, with another December hike as its base case and October still live. BofA asks whether US banks, not Europe's, are the anomaly, citing flattening European curves, deteriorating growth and SX7E's outperformance, and flags SX7E downside (a Dec-26 30D-20D put spread, >4x max payout) as relatively cheap tail protection despite elevated bank put skew. Separately, Goldman's Robert Quinn notes non-dealers bought ~$3bn of Russell 2000 futures in September from multi-year-low positioning, leaving open whether that marks a reversal or gets overwhelmed by deteriorating credit.
